topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and sets out the learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: intrinsic mutations, environmental exposures, and epidemiological evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental origins of cancer by examining the interplay between intrinsic genetic mutations, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens drive malignant transformation, highlighting the specific mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and metabolic activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms by which chemical and physical mutagens induce DNA damage and bulky adducts, often through xenobiotic metabolism.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, two-stage carcinogenesis, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the concept of tumor promotion distinct from initiation, including the Berenbaum two-stage model and host developmental vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Methodologies for detecting carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the epidemiological, genomic, in vivo, and in vitro strategies used to detect carcinogenic substances and evaluate risk.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing and final summary of the lecture.
